steps: A real saved-directory reply arriving after close/reopen cannot populate or edit the new session.
Saved member choices do not auto-select an assembly or change text; three-language selection and Cancel preserve all prepared author bytes.

Reading and choosing preserve an approved ordinary review. Explicit member/action insertion revokes review; Check and Apply change only the draft, ordinary Save retains exact BOM/CRLF in the one intended behavior file.
Eleven local instance identities include three independent instances of one shared crystal definition. A real insertion recheck arriving after a binding switch cannot fill either binding.
Ordinary Save changes exactly the two prepared behavior manifests; page reload/reopen retains all three selected string values, and the saved assembly still captures a valid build plan.
limitations: Actual Chrome and Studio HTTP editor over a disposable copy of the existing reference-game workspace. Not from-blank UI creation, installed Tauri or Android acceptance.

Two copied manifests are prepared with unresolved ordinary strings, and the start source has BOM/CRLF. The browser repairs those fields by explicit choices, review and ordinary Save; canonical author bytes remain untouched.
Member IDs, local instance IDs and saved custom action names remain ordinary strings. No automatic parameter meaning, runtime references, new actions or built-in keyboard mapping is claimed.

Real HTTP replies are delayed to test stale session/binding protection. No catalog response is fabricated. The final saved assembly plan is checked; native gameplay and independent distribution are outside this browser check.
